_about: Catalogue of unsolved historical ciphers not on the Tomokiyo, Schmeh or Dunin lists. Scores are 1-5 and unvalidated: importance = historical weight of what the text could add; solvability = odds of a full reading with the material available online; difficulty = technical work needed (1 trivial key alignment, 5 statistics-only on an unknown system). Priority is computed on the page from adjustable weights. Class A = siblings with decipherment in the same volume, B = partial key or known family in print, C = no key, no sibling. seen: image = leaf viewed on the Gallica image; catalogue = selected from the catalogue description only. outcome: set once an entry has been taken to the leaf here (read, partly read, resolved, closed, or attempted-open); entries with an outcome other than attempted-open leave the open ranking.

entries.title: Mondoucet (Brussels) to Charles IX
entries.status: Read 17 Sept 2026. The only despatch of the ~20 ciphered ones without a Court decipherment; on no list. Four aligners had failed because an unvalidated glyph segmenter split many letters into two components, faking a 1.3–1.4 glyph-per-letter ratio; at glyph level it is an ordinary homophonic substitution, one glyph per letter, four nulls {*, C, mq, j}. Key built by hand from the 16 July crib (ff. 62–64): the f. 62r interlinear glosses ('pouvez', 'leur délivrance', 'au 30') and the verbatim f. 64 reading, anchored HMM alignment, then a French 5-gram beam decoder. Partly enciphered: clear bands give Spanish troop counts before Mons and German levies at Maastricht, with the sign-off 'De Bruxelles ce [Ve] jour de Juillet 1572 / de Mondoucet'; cipher lines J1–J22, K1, M1–M6 read in stretches (religieuse, Espaigne, le pape, Escosse, Angleterre, 'le prince… service du roi', 'parenté entre les autres cour[s]', 'avaient esté capitulé… réduit').
entries.why: Four days before Genlis's relief column was destroyed at Saint-Ghislain; French covert support of Orange six weeks before St Bartholomew.
entries.score_note: Scored as first assigned; the item is read, see the write-up. Decisive control is internal: decoding the 16 July block with the recovered key reproduces the decipherer's own gloss verbatim, 'leur delivrance des espagnols a ce moyen'. Residue is transcription-limited on a ~450-year-old microfilm scan.
entries.verify: Retranscribe the ciphered lines to a fixed glyph accuracy; collate the clear bands against the Didier 1891 edition.

entries.title: Mondoucet (Antwerp, Amsterdam) to Charles IX, two letters of 1573
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 16127 ff. 126v–127v (4 Jan); ff. 135r–137v, decipherment ff. 139r–141r (9 Sep)
entries.status: Read in part 18 Sept 2026. Which passages lack a reading, fixed: the 9 Sept letter (not 5 Sept; cipher on ff. 135r–137v, not 138–140, which are the address leaf and the Court's decipherment) has a complete, verbatim reading: 4,735 glyphs of ff. 135r–137r hand-transcribed and aligned letter for letter to ff. 139r–140v (glyph/letter ratio 0.91, no unaligned run longer than a word); the tail f. 137v/f. 141r checked by length only. The 'shortened margin readings' belong to later letters. The one passage without a reading is the 4 Jan 1573 Antwerp letter, 39 cipher lines (1,468 glyphs) on ff. 126v–127v with only four interlinear glosses; ff. 124–125 are the 5 Dec 1572 decipherments. The 9 Sept alignment gives the 1573 key (the 1572 system); a beam decoder with a period-French 5-gram reads a held-out 9 Sept block at 77 % of letters, and decodes the Court's own gloss 'hambourg' at the glossed place on a page the key never saw. About two-thirds of 4 Jan reads in stretches: levies about Cologne and Frankfurt, 'leurs soldats particuliers', 'depuis naguières… seize ou dix-huit', 'soubz ombre de chercher parti', 'desavantaige [et] desservice qu'il fera', 'l'Angleterre avoit… tenir cent [mil]', '[H]ambourg, on croit debvoir servir pareil'; the limit is the transcription of this hand. gallica_sweep/mondoucet/f1573/reading.md.
entries.why: Siege of Haarlem, Alkmaar; Alva's last year in the Netherlands.
entries.score_note: Scored as first assigned. The abridgement suspected in the entry is not there for 9 Sept; the whole gain is the 4 Jan letter.
entries.verify: Re-read the doubtful glyphs of ff. 126v–127v on the strips; match the other three glosses (l. 19, 22, 27–28).

entries.title: Jean du Bellay (London) to Montmorency, five letters — all already in print in clear
entries.correspondents: Jean du Bellay, bishop of Bayonne → Anne de Montmorency
entries.status: Closed 17 Sept 2026 as found already solved: the notice hides the years; Le Grand's Histoire du divorce III (1688) prints the Court's readings of 15 June, 18 Sept, 17 and 27 Oct 1529 (fr. 3078 nos. 5, 17, 19; fr. 3077 no. 18), and fr. 3077 no. 23 is the 28 Oct 1528 letter whose 15 cipher lines Bourrilly and de Vaissière read in 1905 with a key they recovered (Lasry 2022 re-solved it; DECODE R4254 'non-decrypted' is stale). The key also reads the catalogue's 17 Oct 1529 letter (pp. 113–117, four pages of cipher without interlinear) directly from the leaf: 'j'ay esté veoir le Cardinal en ses ennuis, où que l'y ay trouvé le plus grant exemple' = Le Grand III 370; the boxed cross is Wolsey. By-products of the sweep: fr. 3078 no. 3, 16 June 1529 (p. 21, DECODE R3688 non-decrypted, not in Le Grand or L&P), has never been read; its key (Tomokiyo's 'Bayonne's Cipher 1529') was re-derived on the leaf from the interlinear decipherment of the 22 June letter (pp. 25–27), adding B = o and word signs bien, fault, paix, and the block reads in stretches (…semblant [que] madame ne fust … pour conclure … la [name] luy ayt par[lé] … [il] fault envoyé querir pouvoir, il ne fauldroyt oublyer a le faire…), c. 60 % of signs. The opening of 22 Oct 1529 (not in these volumes; copy fr. 3005 f. 165) is 'non déchiffré' in Le Grand and Brewer. Scheurer t. I (1969) unchecked (lending copy).
entries.why: Henry VIII's divorce suit, the sweating sickness, Wolsey's fall (Oct 1529) reported by the French ambassador.
entries.score_note: Item itself closed (in print since 1688/1905). Open by-products: 16 June 1529 block (key known, glyph reading at 4x), 22 Oct 1529 opening in fr. 3005.
entries.verify: Le Grand III pp. 323–381 and Bourrilly 1905 pp. 430–434 against the leaves; Scheurer t. I for 16 June and 22 Oct 1529.

entries.title: Nicolas Raince (Rome) to Montmorency and François I, eight letters
entries.status: Read in part 17 Sept 2026. Tomokiyo's 1526 key re-measured off his table image (reading it by eye had shifted l/m/n one column, and H is an s) and verified glyph for glyph on the leaf; 86 of the ~106 ciphered lines of pp. 29-31 (13 May) and p. 105 (20 Nov) read by hand and set out as running French in raince/trans/reading_edited.txt, gaps left as gaps, plus the clear close of 13 May (Andrea Doria expected at Civitavecchia with six galleys, nine days before Cognac). New from the cipher: the court of Savoye, Castille and the Bourguignons, 'le chemin de Valence', the Admiral of France, the plague in Rome, advices reaching the Imperials by their own people, a man named Pietro Anthonio taken by the palace, and (20 Nov) a pontificate that 'seroit la cause de la totale ruine de sa maison'. Gallica leaf numbers run two apart: they are page numbers on odd pages, not a half-filmed volume.
entries.why: League of Cognac, the Colonna raid on Rome (Sept 1526), prelude to the Sack; Aug 1529 = Cambrai and Bologna.
entries.score_note: Eight letters in presumably one system give enough text for a statistical attack; no key in print that we know of.
entries.verify: Tomokiyo's François I era article; Omont's inventory for a decipherment elsewhere in fr. 2984.

entries.title: Gramont, Cardinal de Mâcon (Rome) and Langeac (Venice) to Montmorency
entries.correspondents: Gabriel de Gramont; Charles Hémard de Denonville; Jean de Langeac → Montmorency
entries.status: Read 18 Sept 2026. All four keys had been reconstructed by George Lasry in 2023 (tables on Tomokiyo's GL.htm) but no plaintext was published; the four letters use four different keys, not three. fr. 3083 no. 8 (Langeac, Venice, 14 Jan [1529], 'Avranches cipher 1'): read in full bar two short groups — Saint-Pol seeks leave from the Signoria, Venice refuses. fr. 3071 no. 7 (Gramont, Rome, 21 July [1530], 'Gramont 1530'): ~85 % — the Pope sends Rodolfo Pio of Faenza to congratulate the King on the return of the Queen and the princes; 8Δ = PAPE, key-ring = ROY identified. fr. 3091 no. 23 (Gramont, Rome, 11 Oct [1529], 'Gramont 1529'): 171 lines wholly in cipher, read in full at 90-95 % per page — Clement VII's dread of a general council and plan to grant-then-stall it, his offer to feign illness on the road to Bologna to wait for Admiral Chabot, soothsayers foretelling his deposition, a dream before leaving Rome, Orange's Florence/Pisa/Livorno deal. fr. 3071 no. 4 (Mâcon, Rome, 11 Apr 1537, 'Mascon's cipher'): ~90 % of the cipher — Paul III's Farnese marriage offer (Vittoria to Cosimo) and threat to declare for the Emperor, the King's Turkish alliance, the King 'amuses himself in Picardy'; codes 20/30/40 = Empereur/pape/roy; the slip f. 9bis is a contemporary decipherment of the f. 9v passage, matching the reading.
entries.why: Charles V's coronation at Bologna; Clement VII's marriage diplomacy; Paul III and the truce of 1537.
entries.score_note: Scored as first assigned; all four letters read, see gramont1529/NOTES.md. No cryptanalysis needed: the keys are Lasry's. Residue is transcription-limited; a few code signs are identified from context only.
entries.verify: Check B. Wirtz-Daviau's edition of Chabot's 1529 embassy for contemporary decipherments of Gramont's letters; collate the loosely read clear text of the Mâcon letter.

entries.title: Del Vasto to Charles V and two intercepted imperial papers
entries.correspondents: Marquis del Vasto → Charles V; anonymous → Charles V; Italian memoir from Madrid
entries.status: No. 10 found already solved: George Lasry (2023), text edited by Tomokiyo (2026, cryptiana GL.htm, 'Gasto-Charles V Cipher 1'). No. 6 is del Vasto's own letter of early Dec 1527 in Lasry's 'Cipher 2'. Lasry's letter-level decryption was checked, and ~40 code groups were identified here from context (doz=Lautreque, deh=la Marca, bog=buelta, dnb=dinero …), giving an edited reading (vasto1527/n6_reading.md). No. 20 is an Italian letter, Madrid 11 Apr 1528, to 'Garbino', in the same code as Hieronimo Ranzo's letters (fr. 2988). The code is initial letter + number with non-alphabetical numbering; the addition sheet and jargon are ff. 48-50v. ~3,900 groups are transcribed, but only the function-word skeleton is recoverable without the key. No French decipherment exists; Clair. 327 ff. 279-280 is an undeciphered copy.
entries.why: Five months after the Sack of Rome, during Lautrec's campaign in Italy.
entries.score_note: Imperial ciphers of the 1520s are homophonic with large nomenclators; three items, two languages, no key.
entries.verify: Check whether the French deciphered these (a decipherment may sit in another volume of the same series).

entries.title: Sormano and de Vaulx (Ferrara) to François I, three letters
entries.correspondents: Gaspare Sormano, Joachim de Vaulx → François I
entries.folio_note: canvas = folio + 4; no. 63's third sheet is bound out of order at f. 123 (docket f. 123v); siblings no. 62 (f. 113, interlinear decipherment) and no. 67 (f. 124, marginal decipherment); no. 64 (f. 117) has no cipher
entries.status: Read (17 Sept 2026), nos. 65 and 66 in full, no. 63 as far as its leaves go. Lasry's 2023 key verified on the glossed control no. 62 and applied at glyph level: 18,273 glyph boxes from ten page sides, clustered and hand-labelled, a k-NN classifier, then every line checked by eye on magnified strips. Additions to the key proved on the leaves: a null (tall looped sign), the crossbarred long-s = e, a DUCA nomenclator (large double circle), and the d/f/ll/cc forms. No. 66 is docketed 'duplicata' and enciphers different passages from no. 65, so the pair cribs itself. Substance: Alfonso d'Este refuses the kingdom of Naples for himself and the captaincy of the French army, will only accept whatever accord the King negotiates for him with the Pope, and pleads the want of provisions; the agents call his difficulties pretexts and fall back on Ercole d'Este and on Trivulzio. No. 63 ends mid-sentence on f. 116v; its last leaf is not at f. 117. The date '28 Feb' for no. 63 is the catalogue's; the letter itself carries none on the leaves seen.
entries.why: Ferrara's defection from France before the Peace of Cambrai.
entries.score_note: Two deciphered siblings within a month; alignment should give the key in an afternoon. Content is minor.
entries.verify: Open nos. 62–67 and confirm the same cipher hand and symbol set.

entries.title: Forget, Matignon and Mayenne despatches: the cipher solved, and nine leaves read
entries.status: Attempted 17-18 Sept 2026, solved. Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-1 was re-derived on the manuscript from the complete f. 14v/f. 15r crib and corrected (ff-ligature = n, doubled-y = ss, Ze = t, crossed 4 = m, he = l, crossed t = u; three near-identical shapes really do stand for i, n and s, which is why the leaves resisted). Decoding is by beam search over per-figure candidate sets against a 6-gram model of period French, then dictionary segmentation. NINE leaves now read, all in that one key: fr. 15572 ff. 78v, 123-124 (four pages), 143r+v, 150, 154, 173, 196, 201 and fr. 15571 f. 177. THE KEY'S BEST CHECK IS NOT STATISTICAL: f. 78v carries a cipher block WITH its decipherment written down the margin - 'De sorte que je presupose ... descharger la Garonne, de quatre places qu'ils y tiennent, qui sont Castets, Ste Bazeille, Caumont et le Mas ... Clerac, Monflanquin ... Montsegur'. Decoding that block with the key returns its own margin ('de sorte que je', 'tiennent qui sont', 'pour trois mois'); aligning and re-estimating scores 106 seeded with the true key against 3-41 for six scrambles of it and 30 from random. Content: f. 154 and f. 173, the army of Guyenne's pay crisis of April 1586 - musters unpaid, captains near sedition, lenders refusing ('qu'ils n'en auroient pas un escu'), the writer bound for 'plus de quarante [mil] escus'; ff. 196/201, a siege report to the King naming 'le mareschal de Matignon' (the first proper name out of the cipher, spelled by figures all but one of which are keyed) with officers lost to sickness including the man 'qui avoit servy de mareschal de camp de l'armee', and 'parce que la ville est grande et mal aisee a assieger' - which confirms Tomokiyo's code 35 = 'parce que' in running text; ff. 123-124, 'Sire, quelque bonne resolution de les secourir ... en Rouergue'; f. 150, Forget to Villeroy, April 1586; fr. 15571 f. 177, Mayenne's design for Gascony, 31 Dec 1585. ff. 196 and 201 carry ONE despatch on two leaves: transcribed independently, 57% of their figures are identical with 8 runs of eight or more (shuffled control 12%, no runs); the 43% that differ show f. 201 is a re-encipherment, not a copy. RETRACTED during the work: a claim that these leaves use three different ciphers. That rested on figure-frequency profiles computed across transcriptions made in different sittings, whose glyph labels had drifted - an artifact of my own bookkeeping, caught by seeding the solver with the true key versus scrambled versions of it. Also retracted: five figure values read off a single 'rouergue' pattern-match. NINE OF THE TEN LEAVES ARE READ; f. 110 is not. It is the same cipher - decoded with the solved key it beats scrambled keys by +2.07 per figure, against +3.80 on f. 154 and +3.06 on f. 124r, which do read - but its hand is far smaller and denser (about a hundred figures to the line, 54 lines, no clear text and no marginal decipherment anywhere on the leaf). 18 lines are transcribed, 975 figures, and nothing reads continuously. The obstacle is measurably transcription rather than cryptanalysis: a solver seeded with the solved key moves 23 of 27 shared labels away from it on this leaf but leaves them alone on leaves that read, so my names for this scribe's shapes do not match the figures the key is keyed on; and a cold solve reaches -2.34 per figure, the score a correct solution gets, while producing no language - which is what fitting an internally consistent but wrong figure-stream looks like. Finishing it needs an exemplar set for this hand, the work already done for the others. f. 123r would also repay re-transcribing.
entries.why: Guyenne front of the eighth war; Matignon against Navarre.
entries.score_note: Keys mostly known; the work is transcription, and the glyph set is confusable, so the decoder has to carry ambiguity.
entries.verify: Done: the f.18/f.19 pairing verified twice, one-key question settled, confusables measured, pipeline scored at 70 % on a baseline. Next: mine ten to fifteen more crib lines to cover h, q, x, y, z and the code groups, widen baseline.py past three lines, then apply to the eight leaves - noting that exemplars do not transfer between hands, so each leaf needs its own matching or a transcription.

entries.title: Charles III of Lorraine to the count of Vaudémont, copy
entries.correspondents: Charles III, duke of Lorraine → François, comte de Vaudémont
entries.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (fol. 109); no. 22 (fol. 31) is the January decipherment
entries.folio_note: canvas = 2 x folio + 9; no. 97 at fol. 109 = canvas 227, no. 22 at fol. 31 = canvas 71; the folio printed before a piece number belongs to it
entries.status: SOLVED 18 Sept 2026. The cipher is broken and the key recovered. Verify step answered NEGATIVELY first: no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment only, with no cipher on the sheet, so the hoped-for crib does not exist in the volume; DECODE record 9444 independently marks no. 22 'Decrypted'. The piece was catalogued as unsolved - DECODE record 9449 is this exact letter and gives its status 'Non-decrypted' - and no key for it has ever been published: checked against DECODE, Tomokiyo's Cryptiana, the Desenclos-Lasry HistoCrypt 2024 paper, the BnF notices for fr. 3620/3621/3622/3995 and Lepage's 1864 edition, which stops in 1591. Seven candidate key sheets in fr. 3995 were examined, including all four whose DECODE profile matched, and all are eliminated on documentary grounds (fol. 32 a jargon dictionary; fol. 83-84 an all-digit cipher that merely lists 'Duc de Lorraine' as entry 46; fol. 98 endorsed as the Parma-Spain cipher; fol. 103 a Nevers-circle key giving three homophones per letter). The break: the cipher glyphs are ORDINARY CURSIVE LETTERFORMS and can be read directly, which makes the shape clustering that failed before unnecessary. Per-line crops at ~1.5x native yield an eye transcription of 1,109 tokens - 1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms and 38 nomenclator figures - with three long internal repeats confirming self-consistency. The random-move annealer used earlier provably cannot solve a cipher of this size: on a control with a KNOWN key it recovered 37-56% of letters at -2.64 while the true key scored -1.62. Replacing it with a steepest-ascent sweep run to convergence and kicked out of local optima recovers known keys at 98.7-99.6%. Two traps closed: free nulls let the search delete hard positions and beat French at -1.70, an artefact of per-character normalisation; and selecting on the unpenalised score picks a degenerate all-e key. The recovered key is stable across seeds and under a locked crib and scores -2.10 per character. It is verified against the manuscript itself: the eight-symbol group that spells 'chasteau' occurs at two independent places in the cipher and Chasteauvillain stands in the CLEAR on the same page, twice. Unprompted, the key also yields munitions (x3), promesses, prisonniers, resolution, secours, quartiers, clairement, commandement, 'conserver la plaine' and 'ramener mon armee ... es quartiers de la Faulche'. Tested against nulls, since a 4-gram search over 44 free parameters can manufacture French from nothing: run unchanged on shuffled ciphertexts of identical symbol frequencies and scored blind on distinct French words of six letters or more, the manuscript yields 33 where five nulls yield 0-3, mean 1.2, at -2.10 against a null mean of -2.73; the blind list independently returns clairement, resolution, paroistre, quartiers, pourtant and secours. It also forces one correction: the decode gives 'chasteauilains' where the name wants 'chasteauuilains', one symbol short, so the crib is eight letters secure and six more probable rather than fifteen proved. The reading is partial: -2.10 matches controls in which 6-12 pairs of distinct glyphs were transcribed as one form, giving 65-75% of letters, so about a quarter of the glyph identifications are still wrong. The limit is now the transcription, not the cryptanalysis. The fourteen nomenclator figures remain unassigned.
entries.why: Lorraine's double game between the League and Henri IV. The ciphered passages carry the military business the clear text only skirts: prisoners and munitions, an order to receive the Duke's commandment and to conserve the plain, Chasteauvillain, and the intention to bring the army back into the quarters of La Fauche, between Neufchateau and Chaumont. The clear text around them has the attempt on Chasteauvillain, munitions promised and undelivered, Chaumont and Buzonville; no. 22's decipherment carries the January business - the Spanish march on Rouen, Mayenne finding the Spaniards resolved on battle, Parma's judgement, then the legate, the Spanish pretensions, Villeroy at Pontoise, the house of Bourbon, Bellievre, and the peace.
entries.score_note: If no. 22's decipherment corresponds to a cipher copy elsewhere in the volume the key falls; otherwise a single copy.
entries.verify: Answered. The ciphered originals are not in fr. 3621; no key is published, and DECODE records the piece as Non-decrypted. Remaining: re-read the 42 per-line crops with the recovered key in hand to correct the barred, dotted and capital variants, which would read the letter through; recover the fourteen nomenclator figures from context or from a second letter in the same cipher; and check the Archives departementales de Meurthe-et-Moselle, where a duplicate or a key would most plausibly survive.

entries.title: Henri IV to Philippe de Béthune (Rome), three letters
entries.correspondents: Henri IV (countersigned Villeroy) → Philippe de Béthune
entries.status: Partly read 17 Sept 2026: the 10 Nov letter (f. 34, no. 8) read in full through its minute in clear (f. 36, the notice's "copie du n° précédent"); the key (Villeroy-office design as in Bazeries' 1599 Béthune cipher: letters with homophones, dotted and comma letters for words, two-digit figures for names) recovered in most letters and some twenty word signs by EM alignment against the minute and the glosses of 8 Nov and 10 Dec; the 9 Nov letter (f. 33, one page in cipher) reads about six words in ten after a 4x re-transcription (doubling sign φ, syllable groups 61 qui 63 re 65 si 68 tout 71 tion found): the Spanish pressure over Don Alexandre's cardinalate; 22 Nov: all four pages (ff. 46r-47v) transcribed in full 17 Sept 2026 (third pass, `bethune/reading_22nov.md`) - clear French alternating with short cipher runs; the King rebukes two persons named by code groups ([20] and [S 12], most likely the cardinals d'Ossat and Joyeuse) for not having "rompu ce coup" in time, orders the pension of the s.r Camaiano paid to "relever le party francois a Rome", promises to receive Barberini favourably, and ends by awaiting the Pope's answer on the baptism of the dauphin; dated at Saint-Germain and countersigned by Villeroy. The cipher runs decode to fragments only: an oracle bound shows the present transcription can yield at most 71 % of the letters while the decoder already reaches 74.5 %, so the glyph reading, not the key or the language model, is the limit, and connected-component and template-alignment segmentation both fail on this hand. The clear text of both open letters should exist in Cinq cents de Colbert 346 (copies of the Bethune embassy despatches, 23 Aug 1601 - 22 Nov 1602; not digitised) and possibly in Halphen's edition of 18 Oct - 24 Dec 1601 (HathiTrust only). Ten thousand écus to Cardinal Aldobrandini for the Peace of Lyon, ten thousand more promised through Sillery's brother, the Duchess of Nemours' arrêt disregarded.
entries.why: Aftermath of the Peace of Lyon, Biron's treason forming, the dauphin's birth.
entries.score_note: Twenty-five deciphered siblings in the same hand and year: the Feuquières method applies directly.
entries.verify: Code groups 44, 45, 62, 66-72 (names) and the 4x retranscription of ff. 33 and 46-47; the glosses of ff. 53 and 56-57 not yet aligned.

entries.status: Read 18 Sept 2026 (conti1649/). Nos. 41–42 (26–27 Mar 1649, to Noirmoutier) were found already read: G. Lasry, 'Armand de Bourbon's Poly-Homophonic Cipher – 1649', HistoCrypt 2023 (miscited there as fr. 3584); re-read here from a fresh transcription with his key, adding 'ne pouvant', 'pour insister' (no. 42) and the B<l>etaigne slip; Tenerande unidentified. No. 43 is NOT the same cipher: a syllabic number code (four interleaved alphabets, five-syllable blocks, underline = reversed syllable, 99–250 nulls) with a contemporary interlinear decipherment that starts only at line 13. The key was rebuilt from ~3,300 glossed groups and the 12 unglossed opening lines (264 groups) read; nine predicted values later confirmed by glosses. The whole mémoire is edited (READING43.md): Conti to Laigue, 5 March 1649, the day after Rueil opened, promising the Archduke to break the conference the moment he enters France. Four short blotted places open. Write-up docs/conti1649.html.

entries.title: Phelipeaux d'Herbault to Béthune
entries.correspondents: Raymond Phelipeaux d'Herbault → Philippe de Béthune
entries.folio_note: canvas = folio + 5; no. 25 at ff. 69-71 (canvases 74-76), no. 26 at ff. 72-74 (canvases 77-79)
entries.status: Resolved and read (18 Sept 2026). The verify step answered in the affirmative: no. 26 is NOT a second letter but the same letter of 13 Feb 1626, carrying the same cipher with the plaintext written between the lines by a contemporary decipherer. The clear text of the two copies runs word for word and the cipher stands at the same points; no. 25's first run opens 'to 92 ... 17 ... 43' and its third ends '... 68 93 ...' exactly as no. 26's does. So no. 25 was never an undeciphered text: its reading has lain three folios away since 1626. Letter read in full (herbault1626/ct/letter_13feb1626.md). Cipher is a nomenclator of 1-3 character groups mixing figures and letter-forms, about 18 groups per 48 letters; the key table is not tabulated and is not needed, and ~30 further glossed letters of 1625-26 in the same cipher sit in the same volume.
entries.why: The Valtelline settlement (Treaty of Monzon, March 1626). The ciphered passages are the sensitive ones: the Legate's departure for Spain and 'le Pape pour l'acheminement de ces troupes in la Valteline', the fear 'sy le Pape entroit dans la partialite'; the peace with the Huguenots because 'les affaires de cet estat avoyent besoing de ce relasche, et que le faix d'une double guerre ne se pouvoit plus supporter'; the withdrawal of the Dutch ships and the Huguenot admiral following 'avec le reste de sa flotte' by order of the States and without the King's permission; and the prince of Piedmont's propositions, which 'tendent a engager le Roy a la guerre avec l'Espagne, (et que) la Seigneurie de Venize contribue comme faict l'Angleterre et Holande' - the Savoyard push that Monzon defeated six weeks later.
entries.score_note: Trivial key recovery; the same day's second letter (no. 26) is deciphered.
entries.verify: Answered: no. 26 is the same letter with the decipherment. Open to do: tabulate the key from the ~30 glossed letters of 1625-26 in this volume.

entries.title: Garcia de Toledo to Philip II, duplicate ciphered despatch (Great Siege of Malta)
entries.correspondents: Garcia Alvarez de Toledo, viceroy of Sicily and capitan general del Mar → Philip II (in manos del secretario Francisco de Eraso)
entries.folio_note: 6 images: ff. 1r, 1v, 2r, 2v, address leaf (twice); ViewImage.do route, max 915 px
entries.status: Solved 18 Sept 2026. Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 12–43 in plain alphabetical order (vowels and u/v three figures each, consonants one, no nulls, no nomenclator), used inline in otherwise-clear Spanish; 1,930 figure groups, read end to end. Broken from clear-text cribs: the run after 'los' is *seiscientos*, the run after 'puso' is *en tiera*; the alphabetical order then predicted f=21, x=41, y=42, z=43, each confirmed on *effetos*, *baxeles*, *yban*, *plazer*. Content: the 600 soldiers Cardona landed all entered Il Borgo safely; La Valette wept embracing them; a forbidden sortie killed 200 Turks; a second relief run was waved off by the Grand Master's fire-signals four miles from the harbour mouth and the galleys slipped back to sea (reported by *Mosiur de Lenni* = Andrea Provana di Leinì, with Çanoguera piloting); Turkish lines 'seven, eight and ten palms high', 1,500 Turks at the water, sickness in the Ottoman camp; Algiers squadron off Cabo Bono; 40,000 escudos a month for the ships, half of 48,000 ducados already spent, fortification of Syracuse and Augusta; 'El estar sin galeras me destruye'.
entries.why: The viceroy's own account, a week after the Piccolo Soccorso, of a failed second relief of Birgu and of what Sicily could and could not pay for. Tomokiyo's unsolved pages do not list it and PARES records no decipherment.
entries.score_note: Solved; kept for the record.
entries.verify: Done: images on PARES, figures transcribed digit for digit in toledo1565/transcription.txt, all 1,930 groups inside 12–43, all 32 codes used, no odd-length runs.
